adjustedProfit.title: Reported vs adjusted operating profit & EBITDA
adjustedProfit.content:
Croda reports adjusted operating profit and adjusted EBITDA alongside the IFRS/reported figures, excluding exceptional items such as restructuring charges, impairments and acquisition costs.

For Croda International Plc: the 2023-2025 destocking-driven downturn hit the reported lines much harder than the adjusted lines -- reported operating income fell to £110.1m in FY2025 against adjusted operating profit of £295.3m, a gap exceptional items alone explain. Reading the reported figures in isolation overstates how far the underlying business actually fell.

What to watch:

  • The size of the reported/adjusted gap each year -- a shrinking gap signals the destocking-related exceptionals are working through
  • Adjusted EBITDA margin versus reported margin, to isolate the underlying operating trend from one-off charges

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Croda International Plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Croda International Plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Croda International Plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: Reported EPS vs Adjusted EPS
epsDps.content:
EPS (reported) is IFRS net income per share, after exceptional items. Adjusted EPS is Croda's own non-IFRS measure, which strips out exceptional and acquisition-related items to show underlying trading performance. Both are in pence.

For Croda International Plc: reported EPS fell further than adjusted EPS through the FY2023-FY2024 destocking downturn because large exceptional charges (impairments, restructuring) sat only in the reported line. Adjusted EPS is the figure management and most analysts use to track the underlying recovery.

What to watch:

  • Whether the gap between the two lines is narrowing as exceptional items fade
  • A persistently wide gap can mean "exceptional" costs are becoming routine

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Croda International Plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Croda International Plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Croda International Plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Croda International Plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Croda International Plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Croda International Plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
